title: Choose Zedu marketing experiments with explicit hypotheses and stopping rules
description: Create a shared experiment decision process so marketing effort follows evidence. Reuse the existing attribution plan and baseline data where available. Deliver a ranked backlog of five distinct tests, each with audience, hypothesis, primary measure, guardrail, required access, effort, decision threshold and stopping/review rule. Include a results template separating observation from causal claims and a worked synthetic example. Done when the team approves the backlog and can explain continue/change/stop decisions without relying on vanity metrics. Mark low traffic or missing instrumentation as limitations; do not invent lift or guarantee significance. No live experiment, tracking change or ad spend is authorized by this goal.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Build the backlog from tests already half-set-up in this project, and be honest about traffic limits
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Several candidate tests already have work behind them: the search-ad plan for education buyers, the UTM-tagged sign-up tracking goal, the homepage title and H1 fixes, and the store QR codes. Plan: 1) shortlist five distinct tests from those, each with audience, hypothesis, primary measure, a guardrail (for example sign-up completion, not clicks), the access it needs, effort, a decision threshold and a stop or review date; 2) estimate whether current traffic can detect the effect at all, and where it can't, say so and use a longer window or a qualitative read instead of claiming significance; 3) a results template that separates what was observed from what caused it, and a worked synthetic example. Tasks: ranked backlog with thresholds (research), results template and example (content).

upvotes.reason: "Build the backlog from tests already half-set-up in this project, and be honest about traffic limits" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.

Estimating whether current traffic can detect an effect at all, and saying so when it cannot, is what separates a test that decides something from one that produces a number nobody can interpret - with Zedu's traffic today, several of these tests would run for weeks and still be unable to tell a real lift from noise, and naming that up front is worth more than a confident result later. Shortlisting from the tests already half-set-up (the ad plan, the UTM sign-up tracking, the title and H1 fixes, the store QR codes) also means the effort goes into running tests rather than re-planning them, and a guardrail of sign-up completion rather than clicks keeps the measure on the thing that pays.
I support the traffic-limit check and stopping rules; it makes the experiment backlog decision-ready while preventing click counts or small samples from being presented as proof.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Pre-register every test in a one-page log before launch, and publish the result even when it is null
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Without a record written before launch, hypotheses and success measures quietly shift after the data arrives. Approach: a one-page pre-registration per test (hypothesis, primary measure, guardrail, minimum sample or end date, decision rule) dated and shared before launch, then a result entry in the same log whatever the outcome, including "no detectable difference". Done: the template, the five backlog tests pre-registered, and the rule that a test without a pre-registration entry doesn't count. This keeps the backlog honest at Zedu's low traffic.

The accepted workstream builds the backlog but does not fix a hypothesis or stopping rule before launch. A dated, one-page pre-registration that also records null results is what keeps low-traffic tests honest. It adds governance to the existing backlog rather than replacing it.
At low traffic, hypotheses shift after the data arrives unless written first. A dated pre-registration with a decision rule, and publishing null results, keeps the backlog honest.
Hypotheses written after the data arrives are not hypotheses. Pre-registering the test and publishing null results keeps the experiment programme honest.
Without a record written before launch, hypotheses shift after the data arrives; pre-registration is the difference between a test and a story.
